title: GWOSC: gravitational-wave open data, event releases, quality flags, and reanalysis rail
summary: Infrastructure record for GWOSC as a rail that makes gravitational-wave event data, metadata, tutorials, quality flags, and catalog releases available for external analysis. It is encoded as a visibility/reanalysis rail, not as a correctness engine.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0022 after GW150914 surviving-anomaly control pass.

time.event_release_context: GW150914 event release and broader O1/O2 data-release documentation

subjects.name: event strain data, metadata, tutorials, catalogs, data quality and injection flags

claims.claim: LIGO’s data-access page describes GWOSC as fulfilling NSF LIGO’s commitment to release, archive, and serve gravitational-wave data to the broader scientific community and public, and to provide information and tools for understanding and using the data.
what_would_change_status: The official LIGO data page changes or removes this description of GWOSC.

claims.claim: The GW150914 event release page contains a dataset DOI, event timing, false-alarm and detector context, discovery-paper links, and downloadable strain data products around the event, including 32-second and 4096-second windows at 4096 Hz and 16384 Hz.
what_would_change_status: The GWOSC event page changes the data-release or DOI status.

claims.claim: The open-data methods paper says public GWOSC data are validated before release, include data-quality and injection bookkeeping, and require caution because gravitational-wave detector data remain complex and can still contain transient noise artifacts.
what_would_change_status: A later GWOSC methods paper changes the validation/quality/injection/caution picture.

evidence_refs.locator: turn511885view2 L1020-L1033; turn622011view2 L1203-L1228; screenshot turn976245view0

claims.claim: As infrastructure, GWOSC turns anomaly correction and confirmation into inspectable data motion; it does not prove correctness, replace detector characterization, or guarantee exact reproduction of internal collaboration workflows.
what_would_change_status: A future infrastructure audit shows GWOSC should be recoded as a stronger reproducibility rail or a weaker discovery-only rail.

evidence_refs.support_type: rail scope and limits encoded in this record

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official event/data page plus open-data methods extraction
limitations: No data files downloaded or checksummed locally.
No review of GWOSC API or data-management plan beyond first-pass sources.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: validated gravitational-wave strain data, event metadata, quality flags, injection flags, tutorials, catalogs, and downloadable analysis products
outputs: event data releases with DOI surfaces
data quality and injection flag metadata

Does not make every internal workflow exactly reproducible.
Requires domain knowledge, quality flags, and detector-noise caution.

handling_notes: Open data should be credited as public-good infrastructure without overclaiming reproducibility completeness.

No extraction of full data-management plan or API documentation.
